summary: Develop FIDIC claims, donor procurement, and infrastructure risk skills. Build practical controls and action plans. Enquire about the course.
lede: Contract and risk management for donor-funded infrastructure projects helps experienced practitioners coordinate procurement, contract administration, and delivery risks. Participants learn to interpret FIDIC obligations, review donor procurement records and approval controls, and assess claims, delays, cost exposure, and risk allocation. They also practice maintaining compliance and claims matrices and turning project data into performance reports and escalation plans.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate donor procurement, FIDIC contract administration, infrastructure delivery, and risk decisions across multiple institutions. It suits experienced practitioners who already work with project records or contract processes and need an integrated, advanced perspective rather than an introductory explanation of construction contracts.
modules: Donor Project Reporting and Action Planning
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in infrastructure procurement, construction contract administration, project delivery, engineering supervision, legal review, or project implementation unit operations. Prior exposure to FIDIC contracts or donor procurement is strongly recommended, but you do not need specialist programming skills. Bring a redacted contract, risk register, procurement file, schedule, or claims example if organizational policy permits. Exercises use provided materials when confidential records cannot be shared. Advanced digital topics receive operational application treatment, while AI-assisted review and dashboard configuration remain guided exercises rather than production system implementation.
